### Solutions

- **[id 240]**: John has 54 candies, so Robert has $54 / 2 = 27$. James has $27 + 6 = 33$. John has $54 - 33 = 21$ more candies than James.
- **[id 241]**: Dolly reads 2 + 1 = 3 books. Pandora reads 1 + 2 = 3 books. Collectively, they read $3 + 3 = 6$ books.
- **[id 242]**: Mike has $5 - 2 = 3$ pen pals. Each sends $2 \times 5 = 10$ pages per week, totaling 30 pages. He writes 30 pages at 6 minutes per page = 180 minutes = 3 hours per week.
- **[id 243]**: Boss calls use $15 \times 30 = 450$ minutes. Other calls use 300 minutes. Total used = 750 minutes. Remaining = $1000 - 750 = 250$ minutes.
- **[id 244]**: Starting with 24 fries: Kyle takes 5 (19 left), Billy takes 10 (9 left). Colby takes $5 - 3 = 2$ fries. If $9 + G - 2 = 27$, then $G = 20$ fries.
- **[id 245]**: Snail difference is $32 - 4 = 28$. Total fish in both aquariums is $28 / 2 = 14$. Each aquarium has $14 / 2 = 7$ fish.
- **[id 246]**: Total hours = $6 \times 4 \times 5 = 120$ hours. Base cost = $120 \times 250 = \$30,000$. After a 10% discount, Jean pays $\$30,000 \times 0.90 = \$27,000$.
- **[id 247]**: Total cost = $12 + 43 + 15 + 4 + 22 = \$96$. Split 3 ways: $96 / 3 = \$32$ per person.
- **[id 248]**: Total weight = $4 \times 50 = 200$ pounds. Total cost = $200 \times 1.50 = \$300$.
- **[id 249]**: Sue eats $4 \times 5 = 20$ cookies on Monday and $2 \times 13 = 26$ cookies on Tuesday (46 total). Her sister eats $5 + 13 = 18$ cookies. Sue consumes $46 - 18 = 28$ more cookies, which is $28 \times 200 = 5600$ calories.
